## Appendix A: Pre-release checklist

Every recommendation in the book, 192 in all, as one line you can tick. Work through it before you release a design. Each line links to the full recommendation, which gives the reasons and the numbers. These are recommendations, not rules: where you choose not to follow one, it helps to tell your manufacturer why.

### Part 1: The design package (what you send)

#### [Fabrication data](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-008:** [Send one complete fabrication package, in one format, from one revision](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-008-send-one-complete-fabrication-package-in-one-format-from-one-revision)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-009:** [Always send a netlist, made from the same revision as the Gerbers](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-009-always-send-a-netlist-made-from-the-same-revision-as-the-gerbers)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-010:** [Tell the fab where you join nets on purpose](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-010-tell-the-fab-where-you-join-nets-on-purpose)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-011:** [Separate plated and non-plated holes, and use an unambiguous drill format](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-011-separate-plated-and-non-plated-holes-and-use-an-unambiguous-drill-format)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-012:** [Dimension the holes that matter, with their real tolerance](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-012-dimension-the-holes-that-matter-with-their-real-tolerance)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-013:** [Put your intent in the data, not in a note that contradicts it](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-013-put-your-intent-in-the-data-not-in-a-note-that-contradicts-it)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-014:** [Put everything the Gerbers can't say on the fabrication drawing](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-014-put-everything-the-gerbers-cant-say-on-the-fabrication-drawing)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-015:** [Check a copied fabrication drawing line by line](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-015-check-a-copied-fabrication-drawing-line-by-line)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-016:** [Clear every design-rule error before you make the outputs](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/01-fabrication-data/#pcb-dfm-016-clear-every-design-rule-error-before-you-make-the-outputs)

#### [Assembly data](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/02-assembly-data/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-064:** [Always send the XY file, and send native design files and the schematic when you can](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/02-assembly-data/#pcb-dfa-064-always-send-the-xy-file-and-send-native-design-files-and-the-schematic-when-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-065:** [Draw footprints to the IPC zero rotation, and write your convention down](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/02-assembly-data/#pcb-dfa-065-draw-footprints-to-the-ipc-zero-rotation-and-write-your-convention-down)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-066:** [Give every part a unique reference designator, placed next to its own part](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/02-assembly-data/#pcb-dfa-066-give-every-part-a-unique-reference-designator-placed-next-to-its-own-part)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-067:** [Put everything the data can't show on an assembly drawing](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/02-assembly-data/#pcb-dfa-067-put-everything-the-data-cant-show-on-an-assembly-drawing)

#### [The BOM](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/03-bom/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-068:** [Give every BOM line the designators, quantity, maker and full part number](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/03-bom/#pcb-dfa-068-give-every-bom-line-the-designators-quantity-maker-and-full-part-number)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-069:** [Say which lines are locked to one part, and why; list alternates for the rest](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/03-bom/#pcb-dfa-069-say-which-lines-are-locked-to-one-part-and-why-list-alternates-for-the-rest)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-070:** [Check every value and part number before release, and check each part is still made](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/03-bom/#pcb-dfa-070-check-every-value-and-part-number-before-release-and-check-each-part-is-still-made)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-071:** [Mark do-not-place and customer-supplied lines clearly](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/03-bom/#pcb-dfa-071-mark-do-not-place-and-customer-supplied-lines-clearly)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-072:** [For small builds, keep the number of unique BOM lines down](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/03-bom/#pcb-dfa-072-for-small-builds-keep-the-number-of-unique-bom-lines-down)

#### [Footprints and the component library](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-029:** [Use proven footprints for chip resistors and capacitors](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-029-use-proven-footprints-for-chip-resistors-and-capacitors)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-030:** [Use one footprint per package size, not one per part maker](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-030-use-one-footprint-per-package-size-not-one-per-part-maker)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-031:** [Check every footprint you didn't draw yourself, against the datasheet and a real part](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-031-check-every-footprint-you-didnt-draw-yourself-against-the-datasheet-and-a-real-part)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-032:** [Put a solder mask dam between every pad of a fine-pitch part](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-032-put-a-solder-mask-dam-between-every-pad-of-a-fine-pitch-part)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-033:** [Set the solder mask expansion of fine-pitch pads yourself](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-033-set-the-solder-mask-expansion-of-fine-pitch-pads-yourself)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-034:** [Make pin 1 impossible to miss](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-034-make-pin-1-impossible-to-miss)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-035:** [Mark diode and LED polarity so it can't be misread](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-035-mark-diode-and-led-polarity-so-it-cant-be-misread)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-036:** [Draw the real outline of each part in silkscreen, including anything that hangs over the edge](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-036-draw-the-real-outline-of-each-part-in-silkscreen-including-anything-that-hangs-over-the-edge)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-037:** [Size plated through-holes and their pads from the lead](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfa-037-size-plated-through-holes-and-their-pads-from-the-lead)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-007:** [Don't put copper on non-plated holes](https://opendfx.org/01-design-package/04-footprints/#pcb-dfm-007-dont-put-copper-on-non-plated-holes)

### Part 2: The panel (where fabrication meets assembly)

#### [Why boards are built in panels](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/01-why-panels/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-001:** [Let your manufacturer design the panel, and approve it before you order bare boards](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/01-why-panels/#pcb-dfa-001-let-your-manufacturer-design-the-panel-and-approve-it-before-you-order-bare-boards)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-002:** [Make sure small boards can be panelized, and never send them loose](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/01-why-panels/#pcb-dfa-002-make-sure-small-boards-can-be-panelized-and-never-send-them-loose)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-003:** [Expect panels of about 200 × 150 mm, and plan quantities in whole panels](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/01-why-panels/#pcb-dfa-003-expect-panels-of-about-200--150-mm-and-plan-quantities-in-whole-panels)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-004:** [Keep panels stiff: small panels for thin boards, and no long floppy rows](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/01-why-panels/#pcb-dfa-004-keep-panels-stiff-small-panels-for-thin-boards-and-no-long-floppy-rows)

#### [Rails, tooling holes and fiducials](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-005:** [Expect rails along the long edges unless you design them out](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-005-expect-rails-along-the-long-edges-unless-you-design-them-out)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-006:** [Make fiducials simple copper dots, round or square, with a clear ring around them](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-006-make-fiducials-simple-copper-dots-round-or-square-with-a-clear-ring-around-them)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-007:** [Put at least two fiducials on each board, far apart, on every side that has surface-mount parts](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-007-put-at-least-two-fiducials-on-each-board-far-apart-on-every-side-that-has-surface-mount-parts)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-008:** [If there's room, add local fiducials beside expensive or very fine-pitch parts](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-008-if-theres-room-add-local-fiducials-beside-expensive-or-very-fine-pitch-parts)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-009:** [Don't use drilled holes instead of fiducials](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-009-dont-use-drilled-holes-instead-of-fiducials)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-076:** [Make each fiducial show which side and which corner it is](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-076-make-each-fiducial-show-which-side-and-which-corner-it-is)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-077:** [Print the board's part number and the side on the panel rails](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dfa-077-print-the-boards-part-number-and-the-side-on-the-panel-rails)
- [ ] **PCB-DFT-001:** [Give the board its own tooling holes if it will go into a test fixture](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/02-rails-tooling-holes-fiducials/#pcb-dft-001-give-the-board-its-own-tooling-holes-if-it-will-go-into-a-test-fixture)

#### [Breakaway methods: V-score, tabs and mouse bites](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-001:** [Use straight-edged, rectangular board outlines when you can](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/#pcb-dfm-001-use-straight-edged-rectangular-board-outlines-when-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-010:** [Keep overhanging parts away from breakaway edges, and draw the overhang on the silkscreen](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/#pcb-dfa-010-keep-overhanging-parts-away-from-breakaway-edges-and-draw-the-overhang-on-the-silkscreen)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-011:** [Mark critical edges on a drawing, and leave room around the board in the enclosure](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/#pcb-dfa-011-mark-critical-edges-on-a-drawing-and-leave-room-around-the-board-in-the-enclosure)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-012:** [If you need tabs and a clean outline, recess the edge where each tab joins](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/#pcb-dfa-012-if-you-need-tabs-and-a-clean-outline-recess-the-edge-where-each-tab-joins)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-013:** [Agree the number and position of tabs on round or odd-shaped boards](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/#pcb-dfa-013-agree-the-number-and-position-of-tabs-on-round-or-odd-shaped-boards)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-014:** [Talk to your assembler before panelizing boards thicker than about 2 mm](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/03-breakaway-methods/#pcb-dfa-014-talk-to-your-assembler-before-panelizing-boards-thicker-than-about-2-mm)

#### [Clearance near board and panel edges](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/04-edge-clearance/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-015:** [Keep parts and exposed copper at least 3 mm from the edges, 5 mm if you can](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/04-edge-clearance/#pcb-dfa-015-keep-parts-and-exposed-copper-at-least-3-mm-from-the-edges-5-mm-if-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-002:** [Keep copper back from the board edge, further for V-score than for routing](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/04-edge-clearance/#pcb-dfm-002-keep-copper-back-from-the-board-edge-further-for-v-score-than-for-routing)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-016:** [Keep components back from breakaway edges, and ceramic capacitors further still](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/04-edge-clearance/#pcb-dfa-016-keep-components-back-from-breakaway-edges-and-ceramic-capacitors-further-still)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-017:** [Turn ceramic capacitors and other chip parts near a break line parallel to it](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/04-edge-clearance/#pcb-dfa-017-turn-ceramic-capacitors-and-other-chip-parts-near-a-break-line-parallel-to-it)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-003:** [If copper must run to the board edge, say so](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/04-edge-clearance/#pcb-dfm-003-if-copper-must-run-to-the-board-edge-say-so)

#### [X-outs: accepting panels with a bad board](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/05-x-outs/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-004:** [Accept X-outs unless you have a real reason not to](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/05-x-outs/#pcb-dfm-004-accept-x-outs-unless-you-have-a-real-reason-not-to)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-005:** [Design with margin above the fab's minimums to avoid X-outs in the first place](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/05-x-outs/#pcb-dfm-005-design-with-margin-above-the-fabs-minimums-to-avoid-x-outs-in-the-first-place)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-006:** [Prefer smaller panels for designs that are hard to make](https://opendfx.org/02-the-panel/05-x-outs/#pcb-dfm-006-prefer-smaller-panels-for-designs-that-are-hard-to-make)

### Part 3: Bare board fabrication

#### [Materials and stack-up](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-017:** [Use standard FR-4 unless the product needs something else](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/#pcb-dfm-017-use-standard-fr-4-unless-the-product-needs-something-else)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-018:** [Start from your fab's standard stack-up, or give them what they need to build one](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/#pcb-dfm-018-start-from-your-fabs-standard-stack-up-or-give-them-what-they-need-to-build-one)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-019:** [Specify controlled impedance fully, make the traces easy to find, and leave room to widen them](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/#pcb-dfm-019-specify-controlled-impedance-fully-make-the-traces-easy-to-find-and-leave-room-to-widen-them)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-020:** [Size traces and gaps for the finished copper weight](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/#pcb-dfm-020-size-traces-and-gaps-for-the-finished-copper-weight)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-021:** [Use as few layers as the circuit needs](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/#pcb-dfm-021-use-as-few-layers-as-the-circuit-needs)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-073:** [Expect thin boards to need a carrier during assembly](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/01-materials-and-stack-up/#pcb-dfa-073-expect-thin-boards-to-need-a-carrier-during-assembly)

#### [Inner layers and lamination](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/02-inner-layers-and-lamination/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-022:** [Keep copper 0.25 mm or more from drilled holes on every layer](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/02-inner-layers-and-lamination/#pcb-dfm-022-keep-copper-025-mm-or-more-from-drilled-holes-on-every-layer)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-074:** [On very large boards, expect the fab to scale the outer layers, and tell the assembler](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/02-inner-layers-and-lamination/#pcb-dfa-074-on-very-large-boards-expect-the-fab-to-scale-the-outer-layers-and-tell-the-assembler)

#### [Drilling](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/03-drilling/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-023:** [Give hole sizes as finished sizes](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/03-drilling/#pcb-dfm-023-give-hole-sizes-as-finished-sizes)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-024:** [Keep the aspect ratio at 8:1 or less, and holes 0.25 mm or larger where you can](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/03-drilling/#pcb-dfm-024-keep-the-aspect-ratio-at-81-or-less-and-holes-025-mm-or-larger-where-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-025:** [Use as few different hole sizes as you can](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/03-drilling/#pcb-dfm-025-use-as-few-different-hole-sizes-as-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-026:** [Give every plated hole an annular ring with margin above the IPC minimum](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/03-drilling/#pcb-dfm-026-give-every-plated-hole-an-annular-ring-with-margin-above-the-ipc-minimum)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-027:** [Use microvias and blind or buried vias only when you need them](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/03-drilling/#pcb-dfm-027-use-microvias-and-blind-or-buried-vias-only-when-you-need-them)

#### [Plating](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/04-plating/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-028:** [Know what plating does to your holes and outer copper](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/04-plating/#pcb-dfm-028-know-what-plating-does-to-your-holes-and-outer-copper)

#### [Outer layers](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/05-outer-layers/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-029:** [Avoid acute angles, keep pour clearances to your trace rules, and fan out fine-pitch parts through vias](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/05-outer-layers/#pcb-dfm-029-avoid-acute-angles-keep-pour-clearances-to-your-trace-rules-and-fan-out-fine-pitch-parts-through-vias)

#### [Via treatments](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/06-via-treatments/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-030:** [Tent vias by default, on both sides, if they're 0.3 mm or smaller](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/06-via-treatments/#pcb-dfm-030-tent-vias-by-default-on-both-sides-if-theyre-03-mm-or-smaller)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-031:** [Plug or fill vias that must be sealed, or that would trap chemistry](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/06-via-treatments/#pcb-dfm-031-plug-or-fill-vias-that-must-be-sealed-or-that-would-trap-chemistry)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-032:** [For via-in-pad, fill with non-conductive epoxy and plate over it](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/06-via-treatments/#pcb-dfm-032-for-via-in-pad-fill-with-non-conductive-epoxy-and-plate-over-it)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-075:** [Never put solder mask on thermal vias under a QFN](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/06-via-treatments/#pcb-dfa-075-never-put-solder-mask-on-thermal-vias-under-a-qfn)

#### [Solder mask](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-033:** [Choose green solder mask and white legend unless you have a reason not to](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/#pcb-dfm-033-choose-green-solder-mask-and-white-legend-unless-you-have-a-reason-not-to)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-078:** [Keep a solder mask web between every via and the pad beside it, or tent the via](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/#pcb-dfa-078-keep-a-solder-mask-web-between-every-via-and-the-pad-beside-it-or-tent-the-via)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-034:** [Clear solder mask from non-plated holes by about 0.1 mm, with no thin ring left](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/#pcb-dfm-034-clear-solder-mask-from-non-plated-holes-by-about-01-mm-with-no-thin-ring-left)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-035:** [Expect the fab to trim pads to keep mask dams, and check what they changed](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/#pcb-dfm-035-expect-the-fab-to-trim-pads-to-keep-mask-dams-and-check-what-they-changed)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-079:** [For BGAs, use copper-defined pads unless the part maker says otherwise](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/#pcb-dfa-079-for-bgas-use-copper-defined-pads-unless-the-part-maker-says-otherwise)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-082:** [Join BGA and leadless pads to copper pours with a short trace, not straight into the pour](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/07-solder-mask/#pcb-dfa-082-join-bga-and-leadless-pads-to-copper-pours-with-a-short-trace-not-straight-into-the-pour)

#### [Surface finish](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/08-surface-finish/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-036:** [Always name the surface finish on the fabrication drawing](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/08-surface-finish/#pcb-dfm-036-always-name-the-surface-finish-on-the-fabrication-drawing)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-037:** [Choose ENIG for most boards; lead-free HASL only for coarse pitch; OSP or immersion silver for high volume with tight process control](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/08-surface-finish/#pcb-dfm-037-choose-enig-for-most-boards-lead-free-hasl-only-for-coarse-pitch-osp-or-immersion-silver-for-high-volume-with-tight-process-control)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-038:** [Give edge-connector fingers hard gold and a bevel, with mask and legend kept off them](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/08-surface-finish/#pcb-dfm-038-give-edge-connector-fingers-hard-gold-and-a-bevel-with-mask-and-legend-kept-off-them)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-080:** [Keep bare boards sealed, use them within the finish's shelf life, and expect a bake if they've taken on moisture](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/08-surface-finish/#pcb-dfa-080-keep-bare-boards-sealed-use-them-within-the-finishs-shelf-life-and-expect-a-bake-if-theyve-taken-on-moisture)

#### [Legend (silkscreen)](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-039:** [Make legend text about 1 mm tall, with lines of 0.15 mm or more](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/#pcb-dfm-039-make-legend-text-about-1-mm-tall-with-lines-of-015-mm-or-more)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-040:** [Send only the legend you want printed, keep it off exposed copper, and expect the fab to clip and resize it](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/#pcb-dfm-040-send-only-the-legend-you-want-printed-keep-it-off-exposed-copper-and-expect-the-fab-to-clip-and-resize-it)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-081:** [Leave legend out where it won't fit, but keep it complete in your data](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/#pcb-dfa-081-leave-legend-out-where-it-wont-fit-but-keep-it-complete-in-your-data)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-045:** [Keep legend off vias, even tented ones](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/#pcb-dfm-045-keep-legend-off-vias-even-tented-ones)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-127:** [Turn legend text so it reads from only two edges of the board](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/#pcb-dfa-127-turn-legend-text-so-it-reads-from-only-two-edges-of-the-board)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-128:** [Use a callout box where parts are packed too tightly for their designators](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/09-legend/#pcb-dfa-128-use-a-callout-box-where-parts-are-packed-too-tightly-for-their-designators)

#### [Profiling: routing, scoring, slots and cut-outs](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/10-profiling/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFM-041:** [Draw the outline, slots and cut-outs as closed shapes on one layer](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/10-profiling/#pcb-dfm-041-draw-the-outline-slots-and-cut-outs-as-closed-shapes-on-one-layer)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-042:** [Allow for the router: a radius in every inside corner and slots at least 1 mm wide](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/10-profiling/#pcb-dfm-042-allow-for-the-router-a-radius-in-every-inside-corner-and-slots-at-least-1-mm-wide)
- [ ] **PCB-DFM-043:** [Dimension castellations, edge plating, countersinks and bevels on the drawing, and expect them to cost more](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/10-profiling/#pcb-dfm-043-dimension-castellations-edge-plating-countersinks-and-bevels-on-the-drawing-and-expect-them-to-cost-more)

#### [Bare board electrical test and inspection](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/11-bare-board-test/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFT-002:** [Have every bare board electrically tested against your netlist](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/11-bare-board-test/#pcb-dft-002-have-every-bare-board-electrically-tested-against-your-netlist)
- [ ] **PCB-DFT-003:** [Ask for IPC Class 2 unless the product needs Class 3, and know Class 3 is a design standard too](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/11-bare-board-test/#pcb-dft-003-ask-for-ipc-class-2-unless-the-product-needs-class-3-and-know-class-3-is-a-design-standard-too)
- [ ] **PCB-DFT-004:** [For boards that matter, ask for the fab's evidence](https://opendfx.org/03-bare-board-fabrication/11-bare-board-test/#pcb-dft-004-for-boards-that-matter-ask-for-the-fabs-evidence)

### Part 4: Components and materials

#### [Choosing parts that can be bought and built](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-083:** [Choose parts that are active, widely stocked, and made by more than one maker where you can](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/#pcb-dfa-083-choose-parts-that-are-active-widely-stocked-and-made-by-more-than-one-maker-where-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-084:** [For parts at risk of shortage, give the board a way to take an alternate](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/#pcb-dfa-084-for-parts-at-risk-of-shortage-give-the-board-a-way-to-take-an-alternate)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-085:** [In production, use the original maker's part on reel, not hobby modules or reseller strips](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/#pcb-dfa-085-in-production-use-the-original-makers-part-on-reel-not-hobby-modules-or-reseller-strips)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-086:** [Check that board-mount connectors suit your board thickness and the product](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/#pcb-dfa-086-check-that-board-mount-connectors-suit-your-board-thickness-and-the-product)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-087:** [For LEDs and other parts sold in bins, choose the bin, or test each bin and say how to handle it](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/#pcb-dfa-087-for-leds-and-other-parts-sold-in-bins-choose-the-bin-or-test-each-bin-and-say-how-to-handle-it)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-088:** [Don't name a brand of solder, flux or other process material unless the product needs it](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/01-choosing-parts/#pcb-dfa-088-dont-name-a-brand-of-solder-flux-or-other-process-material-unless-the-product-needs-it)

#### [Packaging: reels, cut tape, tubes, trays](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/02-packaging/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-089:** [Choose tape and reel, and use tubes only as a last resort](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/02-packaging/#pcb-dfa-089-choose-tape-and-reel-and-use-tubes-only-as-a-last-resort)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-090:** [Choose connectors packaged for machine placement: on tape, with a flat top or a pick-up cap](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/02-packaging/#pcb-dfa-090-choose-connectors-packaged-for-machine-placement-on-tape-with-a-flat-top-or-a-pick-up-cap)

#### [Moisture-sensitive parts](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/03-moisture-sensitive-parts/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-091:** [Put each part's moisture sensitivity level on the BOM, from its datasheet](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/03-moisture-sensitive-parts/#pcb-dfa-091-put-each-parts-moisture-sensitivity-level-on-the-bom-from-its-datasheet)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-092:** [Prefer a lower moisture level when you have the choice, and remember a double-sided build uses one floor life for both sides](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/03-moisture-sensitive-parts/#pcb-dfa-092-prefer-a-lower-moisture-level-when-you-have-the-choice-and-remember-a-double-sided-build-uses-one-floor-life-for-both-sides)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-093:** [Expect cheap addressable RGB LEDs and similar parts to need baking, and budget for it](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/03-moisture-sensitive-parts/#pcb-dfa-093-expect-cheap-addressable-rgb-leds-and-similar-parts-to-need-baking-and-budget-for-it)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-094:** [Keep your own moisture-sensitive stock sealed, and let your assembler bake anything that's been exposed](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/03-moisture-sensitive-parts/#pcb-dfa-094-keep-your-own-moisture-sensitive-stock-sealed-and-let-your-assembler-bake-anything-thats-been-exposed)

#### [Sourcing, counterfeits and obsolescence](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/04-sourcing/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-095:** [Buy parts only from authorized distributors or the maker](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/04-sourcing/#pcb-dfa-095-buy-parts-only-from-authorized-distributors-or-the-maker)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-096:** [If you must buy from a broker or an unfamiliar source, ask for traceability, have the parts inspected, and try them on a small build first](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/04-sourcing/#pcb-dfa-096-if-you-must-buy-from-a-broker-or-an-unfamiliar-source-ask-for-traceability-have-the-parts-inspected-and-try-them-on-a-small-build-first)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-097:** [Find your long-lead and single-source parts early and buy them ahead, without hoarding](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/04-sourcing/#pcb-dfa-097-find-your-long-lead-and-single-source-parts-early-and-buy-them-ahead-without-hoarding)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-098:** [Tell your assembler or distributor your expected volumes](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/04-sourcing/#pcb-dfa-098-tell-your-assembler-or-distributor-your-expected-volumes)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-099:** [Don't set a fixed date-code limit; store parts well, and have old or doubtful stock tested for solderability](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/04-sourcing/#pcb-dfa-099-dont-set-a-fixed-date-code-limit-store-parts-well-and-have-old-or-doubtful-stock-tested-for-solderability)

#### [Supplying your own parts (consignment) and spares](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-100:** [Let your assembler buy the parts, and consign only the few you must](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-100-let-your-assembler-buy-the-parts-and-consign-only-the-few-you-must)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-101:** [Send consigned parts ready for the machines](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-101-send-consigned-parts-ready-for-the-machines)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-102:** [Ship consigned parts in static-shielding packaging, and moisture-sensitive ones sealed](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-102-ship-consigned-parts-in-static-shielding-packaging-and-moisture-sensitive-ones-sealed)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-103:** [Label every package with its part number, and every shipment with your order details](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-103-label-every-package-with-its-part-number-and-every-shipment-with-your-order-details)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-104:** [Get consigned parts to the assembler at least the quoted assembly time before the ship date](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-104-get-consigned-parts-to-the-assembler-at-least-the-quoted-assembly-time-before-the-ship-date)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-105:** [Send spares: plenty of cheap parts, at least one of each expensive one, and say when you can't](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-105-send-spares-plenty-of-cheap-parts-at-least-one-of-each-expensive-one-and-say-when-you-cant)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-106:** [Tell your assembler before a substitute part number arrives](https://opendfx.org/04-components-and-materials/05-consignment-and-spares/#pcb-dfa-106-tell-your-assembler-before-a-substitute-part-number-arrives)

### Part 5: Assembly

#### [Solder paste printing and stencils](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/01-solder-paste-and-stencils/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-018:** [Send the paste layer 1:1 with your copper pads](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/01-solder-paste-and-stencils/#pcb-dfa-018-send-the-paste-layer-11-with-your-copper-pads)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-019:** [Put paste on every pad you want soldered, and only those](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/01-solder-paste-and-stencils/#pcb-dfa-019-put-paste-on-every-pad-you-want-soldered-and-only-those)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-020:** [Don't put one very fine-pitch part on a board of large parts](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/01-solder-paste-and-stencils/#pcb-dfa-020-dont-put-one-very-fine-pitch-part-on-a-board-of-large-parts)

#### [Component placement](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/02-component-placement/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-021:** [Use the largest package the board has room for](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/02-component-placement/#pcb-dfa-021-use-the-largest-package-the-board-has-room-for)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-022:** [At fine pitch, choose a BGA or QFN over a leaded QFP](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/02-component-placement/#pcb-dfa-022-at-fine-pitch-choose-a-bga-or-qfn-over-a-leaded-qfp)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-023:** [Leave room around every part, and keep tall parts away from tiny ones](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/02-component-placement/#pcb-dfa-023-leave-room-around-every-part-and-keep-tall-parts-away-from-tiny-ones)

#### [Reflow soldering](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/03-reflow-soldering/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-024:** [On a double-sided board, put small, light parts on one side and heavy parts on the other](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/03-reflow-soldering/#pcb-dfa-024-on-a-double-sided-board-put-small-light-parts-on-one-side-and-heavy-parts-on-the-other)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-025:** [Don't put a few parts on the second side just because there's room](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/03-reflow-soldering/#pcb-dfa-025-dont-put-a-few-parts-on-the-second-side-just-because-theres-room)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-026:** [Check that every part can survive a standard lead-free reflow, and flag any that can't](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/03-reflow-soldering/#pcb-dfa-026-check-that-every-part-can-survive-a-standard-lead-free-reflow-and-flag-any-that-cant)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-027:** [Spread the heat load: don't put huge parts right beside tiny ones](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/03-reflow-soldering/#pcb-dfa-027-spread-the-heat-load-dont-put-huge-parts-right-beside-tiny-ones)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-028:** [Talk to your assembler first about very thin boards and large, heavy double-sided panels](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/03-reflow-soldering/#pcb-dfa-028-talk-to-your-assembler-first-about-very-thin-boards-and-large-heavy-double-sided-panels)

#### [Optical and X-ray inspection](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/04-inspection/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-038:** [Join neighboring pins in copper, and keep a solder mask dam between them](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/04-inspection/#pcb-dfa-038-join-neighboring-pins-in-copper-and-keep-a-solder-mask-dam-between-them)

#### [Through-hole soldering](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-039:** [Use surface mount by default, and through-hole only where a part takes force](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-039-use-surface-mount-by-default-and-through-hole-only-where-a-part-takes-force)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-040:** [Prefer hybrid parts: surface-mount signals with through-hole pegs](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-040-prefer-hybrid-parts-surface-mount-signals-with-through-hole-pegs)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-041:** [Leave room around pin-in-paste parts for extra paste](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-041-leave-room-around-pin-in-paste-parts-for-extra-paste)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-042:** [Choose through-hole parts rated for the soldering process they'll see](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-042-choose-through-hole-parts-rated-for-the-soldering-process-theyll-see)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-043:** [Keep surface-mount parts away from through-hole pins on the solder side](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-043-keep-surface-mount-parts-away-from-through-hole-pins-on-the-solder-side)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-044:** [Use thermal relief on through-hole pads connected to planes](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-044-use-thermal-relief-on-through-hole-pads-connected-to-planes)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-045:** [Match through-hole lead length to the board and the pitch](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-045-match-through-hole-lead-length-to-the-board-and-the-pitch)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-046:** [Choose through-hole parts that hold themselves in place](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/05-through-hole-soldering/#pcb-dfa-046-choose-through-hole-parts-that-hold-themselves-in-place)

#### [Press-fit and mechanical parts](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/06-press-fit-and-mechanical/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-047:** [Talk to your assembler before designing in press-fit parts](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/06-press-fit-and-mechanical/#pcb-dfa-047-talk-to-your-assembler-before-designing-in-press-fit-parts)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-048:** [Give a torque for every screw and nut, and fasten hardware before soldering](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/06-press-fit-and-mechanical/#pcb-dfa-048-give-a-torque-for-every-screw-and-nut-and-fasten-hardware-before-soldering)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-049:** [Avoid soldering a connector made only for press-fit](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/06-press-fit-and-mechanical/#pcb-dfa-049-avoid-soldering-a-connector-made-only-for-press-fit)

#### [Shields, adhesives and underfill](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/07-shields-adhesives-underfill/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-050:** [Choose a two-piece or clip-on RF shield for low volumes, and a one-piece shield for high volumes](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/07-shields-adhesives-underfill/#pcb-dfa-050-choose-a-two-piece-or-clip-on-rf-shield-for-low-volumes-and-a-one-piece-shield-for-high-volumes)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-051:** [Hold heavy parts down against vibration, and fit the hold-down before soldering](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/07-shields-adhesives-underfill/#pcb-dfa-051-hold-heavy-parts-down-against-vibration-and-fit-the-hold-down-before-soldering)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-052:** [Check part numbers so you don't order glue-mounted parts by mistake](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/07-shields-adhesives-underfill/#pcb-dfa-052-check-part-numbers-so-you-dont-order-glue-mounted-parts-by-mistake)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-053:** [Expect adhesive-mounted dome switches to need tooling](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/07-shields-adhesives-underfill/#pcb-dfa-053-expect-adhesive-mounted-dome-switches-to-need-tooling)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-054:** [Consider underfill or corner bonding for BGAs in products that take repeated shock](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/07-shields-adhesives-underfill/#pcb-dfa-054-consider-underfill-or-corner-bonding-for-bgas-in-products-that-take-repeated-shock)

#### [Cleaning](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/08-cleaning/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-055:** [Use no-clean flux unless your product needs cleaning, and say so if it does](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/08-cleaning/#pcb-dfa-055-use-no-clean-flux-unless-your-product-needs-cleaning-and-say-so-if-it-does)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-056:** [If a product works with no-clean, don't add cleaning or change the flux without a reason](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/08-cleaning/#pcb-dfa-056-if-a-product-works-with-no-clean-dont-add-cleaning-or-change-the-flux-without-a-reason)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-057:** [Design boards that need cleaning so the fluid can get underneath](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/08-cleaning/#pcb-dfa-057-design-boards-that-need-cleaning-so-the-fluid-can-get-underneath)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-058:** [Flag parts that can't be washed, and don't wash rigid-flex boards with chemicals](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/08-cleaning/#pcb-dfa-058-flag-parts-that-cant-be-washed-and-dont-wash-rigid-flex-boards-with-chemicals)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-059:** [Keep small boards that need washing in their panel](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/08-cleaning/#pcb-dfa-059-keep-small-boards-that-need-washing-in-their-panel)

#### [Conformal coating](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/09-conformal-coating/)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-060:** [Clean boards before they're coated, where you can](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/09-conformal-coating/#pcb-dfa-060-clean-boards-before-theyre-coated-where-you-can)
- [ ] **PCB-DFA-061:** [Mark on the drawing the areas that must not be coated](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/09-conformal-coating/#pcb-dfa-061-mark-on-the-drawing-the-areas-that-must-not-be-coated)

- [ ] **PCB-DFA-062:** [Ask how flexible boards will be separated](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/10-depaneling/#pcb-dfa-062-ask-how-flexible-boards-will-be-separated)

#### [Rework and repair](https://opendfx.org/05-assembly/11-rework/)
